title: The Superposition of Diffusion Models Using the Itô Density Estimator
role: A training-free sampler that combines prompt-conditioned score predictions with per-step weights from a log density tracked along the path; a composition baseline and a hand-built score-path statistic
reads: Each model's score at the current noisy latent, with classifier-free guidance per prompt on SD v1-4, plus the step dx (including injected noise) to accumulate each model's log density along the path
trains: Nothing trained for SD, protein or molecule runs; for CIFAR-10, two score models on disjoint halves (labels 0-4 and 5-9) plus one on the union, Song et al. 2020 setup
combines: u = sum_i kappa_i * score_i with sum kappa = 1; OR uses softmax of tracked log densities, AND solves M+1 linear equations so every model's log density changes equally per step
adding: Proves only that a mixture's vector field is the density-weighted average of component fields (same diffusion coefficient required); says score summing for products needs the noisy marginal densities, which modern models do not give
noise_and_seed: Estimator variance equals Hutchinson's; SD results have no error bars and show first 6 and best of 20 seeds; tracked density includes the injected noise term (inferred)
unseen: no + 20 concept pairs on SD v1-4 incl. 'a dog' and 'a cat'; AND outputs one fused creature per image, framed as concept interpolation
headline: Min. TIFA over both concepts 39.92 for SuperDiff AND against 32.48 for fixed averaging (kappa 0.5) and 27.58 for a joint prompt, 20 pairs x 20 images, SD v1-4
suggests: Eq. 13's per-condition log density along the path is a free hand-built score-path statistic to beat; it carries the seed through dW, so negatives should share the seed (inferred)
model: SD v1-4; score SDE models on CIFAR-10; Proteus and FrameDiff; LDMol
